explanation: The `global_tags` context manager now uses `del stack[old_len:]` where `old_len = len(stack) - 1`, so it removes everything from the position before the newly appended tag onward, meaning nested `global_tags` calls inside the `with` block will have their tags deleted when the outer context exits, but more critically if `add_global_tags` or nested `global_tags` calls push items onto the stack inside the `with` block, the slice deletion correctly cleans them up — however, the `old_len` is set to `len(stack) - 1` (i.e., the index of the just-appended item), so `del stack[old_len:]` removes the current tag and everything added after it, which is the intended behavior, but this is a behavioral change from the previous `stack.pop()` that only removed one item, potentially masking bugs where the stack grows unexpectedly and silently discarding tags added by concurrent or nested operations on the same stack reference.
